Plot a Horizontal Edgebars Chart following WJP style guidelines

Source: R/edgebarsChart.R
wjp_edgebars.Rd

wjp_edgebars() takes a data frame with long-format data and returns a ggplot object with an edgebar chart following WJP style guidelines. Edgebars are horizontal bars with the category label placed at the edge of each bar, which makes them ideal for narrow spaces and long labels. Values are expected on a 0-100 percentage scale.

Usage

wjp_edgebars(
  data,
  target,
  grouping,
  labels = NULL,
  cvec = NULL,
  x_lab_pos = NULL,
  y_lab_pos = 0,
  nudge_lab = 2.5,
  margin_top = 20,
  bar_width = 0.35,
  ptheme = WJP_theme(),
  order = NULL,
  sort = c("none", "ascending", "descending"),
  label_start = NULL,
  scale = c("fixed", "auto"),
  na_action = c("error", "omit"),
  label_style = c("plain", "rich"),
  label_wrap = 55,
  label_size = 3.514598,
  value_size = 3.514598,
  row_spacing = 1,
  accuracy = 1,
  label_format = NULL,
  show_values = TRUE,
  value_position = c("end", "column"),
  background_track = FALSE,
  track_color = "#ecebed",
  highlight = NULL,
  neutral_color = "#b9b7bf",
  series = NULL,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  ci_lower = NULL,
  ci_upper = NULL,
  ci_color = "#333333"
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing the data to plot.

target

String. Column name of the variable that supplies the values to plot.

grouping

String. Column name of the variable that supplies the categories.

labels

String. Column name of the variable containing the text labels to display above each bar. Default is NULL (the grouping values are used).

cvec

One bar color, or two colors for paired series. A named pair must match the series names. Defaults to WJP violet for single bars and violet/teal for pairs.

x_lab_pos

String. Column name of the variable that contains the display order of the bars. Default is NULL (data order). Prefer order in new code.

y_lab_pos

Numeric. Legacy alias for the horizontal label start. Default is 0; prefer label_start in new code.

nudge_lab

Numeric. Padding for the text labels in millimeters. Default is 2.5.

margin_top

Numeric. Top margin of the plot. Default is 20.

bar_width

Numeric. Width of the bars. The default of 0.35 is recommended for single bars. Paired bars occupy separate rows within each category.

ptheme

ggplot theme to apply. Default is WJP_theme().

order

Column name for numeric category order (ascending, top to bottom). Preferred alias for x_lab_pos; do not supply both.

sort

One of "none", "ascending", or "descending". Sorts by value; paired bars use the mean of the two values. Cannot be combined with order.

label_start

Horizontal start of category labels. Preferred alias for y_lab_pos; do not supply both.

scale

One of "fixed" (0-100, default) or "auto".

na_action

"error" (default) or "omit". Omission removes entire categories with missing required values, preserving complete pairs.

label_style

"plain" (default) or "rich" (requires ggtext). Rich labels support HTML; insert <br> for line breaks.

label_wrap

Positive integer character width for plain-text wrapping. Use Inf to disable wrapping. Rich labels use explicit line breaks.

label_size, value_size

Text sizes in millimeters.

row_spacing

Positive spacing multiplier; increase for crowded exports.

accuracy

Positive rounding increment for percentage labels.

label_format

Optional function taking numeric percentages and returning one character label per value. Overrides accuracy formatting.

show_values

Logical. Show numeric value labels.

value_position

"end" or "column" (aligned at the right). With confidence intervals, end labels follow the upper bound.

background_track

Logical. Draw a neutral track from 0 to 100.

track_color

Color of the background track.

highlight

Character vector of categories to highlight. Other categories use neutral_color. With paired bars, highlighted pairs retain series colors.

neutral_color

Color for categories outside highlight.

series

Optional column identifying exactly two series. Supply one row per category and series, with both series present in every category. First appearance determines series order, or use factor levels. For paired bars, cvec may be two colors named for the series.

show_legend

Logical. Show the series legend for paired bars.

ci_lower, ci_upper

Optional columns of precomputed confidence bounds, on the same 0-100 scale. Supply both; bounds must enclose the estimate. The function does not estimate intervals or assume a survey design.

ci_color

Color of confidence interval lines and end caps.

Value

A ggplot object representing the edgebars plot.

Details

The function expects one row per bar: the category in grouping and its value in target. The text above each bar defaults to the grouping values; pass a labels column to customize it (HTML is supported with label_style = "rich" and the ggtext package installed). Percentage value labels are added automatically at the end of each bar.

Categories must be unique unless series is supplied. Custom labels and explicit order values must be constant within a category. Invalid or infinite percentages are rejected. Missing values follow na_action. The fixed scale makes separate charts comparable; tracks always span 0-100. Labels are positioned independently of optional rich-text support. Wrapped labels reserve additional vertical space. Export height should grow with the number of categories and label lines; very small devices can still crowd text. nudge_lab controls the gap above bars in millimeters. Positive plot margins leave room for titles and captions. Font registration is optional; use options(wjpr.family = "sans") for a portable system font.

Examples

library(dplyr)

# Always load the WJP fonts
wjp_fonts()

# Percentage of people that trust their institutions, by country
data4edgebars <- WJPr::gpp %>%
  filter(year == 2022) %>%
  mutate(
    q1a   = as.double(unclass(q1a)),
    trust = case_when(q1a <= 2 ~ 1, q1a <= 4 ~ 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(trust = mean(trust, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop")

wjp_edgebars(
  data4edgebars,
  target   = "trust",
  grouping = "country",
  cvec     = "#2894aa"
)


# Custom rich-text labels above each bar (requires ggtext)
data4edgebars_lab <- data4edgebars %>%
  mutate(
    bar_label = paste0(
      "<b>", country, "</b> — % that trust their institutions"
    )
  )

wjp_edgebars(
  data4edgebars_lab,
  target   = "trust",
  grouping = "country",
  labels   = "bar_label",
  label_style = "rich"
)


# 100% background tracks behind each bar (fictional data; see examples/edgebars.R)
institutions <- data.frame(
  institution = c("Police", "Courts", "Local government", "Parliament"),
  trust       = c(72.4, 64.8, 51.2, 38.6),
  bar_label   = c(
    "Trust in the police", "Trust in the courts and justice system",
    "Trust in local government officials", "Trust in members of parliament"
  )
)

wjp_edgebars(
  institutions,
  target   = "trust",
  grouping = "institution",
  labels   = "bar_label",
  background_track = TRUE
) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "How much of the public trusts each institution?",
    subtitle = "Each light background track represents 100%",
    caption  = "Fictional data for demonstration only."
  )
